summary: A familiar top 10 with a good spread: Ronaldo, Messi, LeBron and Curry come easily, Canelo at #2 and Hamilton at #10 are the surprises. Old stars are now free, so a casual player finds 6 with lives to spare.
reasons: Casual found 6 in 14 guesses (Ronaldo, Messi, LeBron, Curry, Ohtani, Durant) and lost 2 lives, on Neymar (#7 in 2024) and Mbappe (#6 in 2024, through the confirm box). Tiger, McGregor, Djokovic, Mahomes, Jake Paul and Haaland were free. Canelo, Rahm, Benzema and Hamilton feel fair when revealed.

A fan who leads with last year's list burns out: Fury, Usyk (confirm box), Prescott, Burrow and Soto took all 5 lives at guess 11, with 6 found and Benzema, Durant and Rahm still to come. Each miss shows its 2025 or 2024 figure, so they are near misses you learn from, but the list rewards knowing this year's changes.

Title and prompt name Forbes' 2026 list and the measure, the top 10 matches the page, every answer has a fact, and category words (forbes, nba, boxing, golf, f1, real madrid) give nothing away. Not Blitz-ready: only the 10 answers score.
fixes: "john rahm" and "jhon rahm" are not recognized: the game tells a player who knows #7 that he isn't an answer ("rahm" and "jon ram" work). Add "John Rahm" as an alias (scripts/intent.ts). The class is in the matcher (src/game/match.ts, coordinator): with the surname shared, "john" vs "jon" is compared alone at length 3, which gets no typo budget.

Unranked answers match only their full name: "fury" and "burrow" say "isn't an answer for this list" while "tyson fury" and "joe burrow" cost a life with a figure. Give the extras the surname short forms the top 10 get (only Giannis has aliases now), so the reveal is true either way.
